messages:
anya: quick RFC follow-up — we should formalize a tiny adapter contract between precision profiles and the runtime. need explicit fields: preference, min_quality, fallback_order, and a place for per-model calibration pointers. anyone object?

mike: +1, sounds useful. runtime needs ability to override preference for capacity/latency reasons (eg force int8 during bursts).

kai: agree. we also need telemetry hooks so we can record per-request quality signals and trigger regressions. simple fields in the contract will help.

sara: product note: defaults must be sane. if a request fails quality, should we 400, or return degraded result with header? prefer soft degrade + explicit header so caller can opt-in to strict mode.

mike: quick config sketch: ```json
{
  "precision_profile": "auto",
  "min_quality_score": 0.92,
  "fallback_order": ["fp8", "int8", "4bit"],
  "strict_mode": false
}
```

anya: nice. min_quality_score should map to eval harness metric (ROUGE/accuracy/other) per model. store mapping in the profile metadata.

kai: question: where do we store per-model calibration blobs and sample prompts? embedding in model artifact is heavy. prefer a lightweight profile service referencing blobs by id. runtime can fetch asynchronously and cache.

mike: agree, profile service + TTL cache in runtime. keep it optional — fallback to default heuristics if profile missing.

sara: product asks for an API-level pin: callers can pass prefer_precision or pin_precision to guarantee no runtime reordering. but warn about capacity errors.

anya: proposal: contract fields = {preference, pin_precision, min_quality_score, fallback_order, calibration_ref}. runtime policy: honor pin_precision unless capacity/strict_mode conflicts; otherwise return 429 or degrade based on strict_mode.

kai: add headers/tracing: X-Redwood-Precision, X-Redwood-Quality-Score, and trace id to link to eval samples. also emit metric tags for profile_id and actual_precision_used.

mike: ops note: implement a soft-canary that flips strict_mode for small % of traffic and compares quality escrow. we need automatic rollback when delta > threshold.

sara: +1 on quality escrow. expose a lightweight webhook/alert when regressions observed.

deploy-bot: created gh issue redwood/inference#345: "adapter-contract: precision profile schema + runtime shim" and assigned to @anya.

anya: plan: I'll open a PR with schema + runtime shim README. target canary next week. if nobody objects I'll draft the PR today.

mike: go for it. happy to help with runtime shim.

kai: i'll add telemetry hooks in the pipeline.

sara: product will prep canary acceptance criteria.

anya: thanks all. keeping this small will make it easier to iterate. :rocket:
